message.content:
# Case PA-OVERLAP — Single-Issuer Policy vs. an Incomplete Holdings Map

**Scope note:** This is a historical research exercise on a fictional long-only US equity portfolio. It is not a real account, not a trade recommendation, and no ledger records were created or modified. All issuer facts below come from the frozen offline SEC-source adapter (`FINTECH-SEC-SCREEN-HOLDOUT-v1`, as_of 2026-10-22T12:51:27Z), which is explicitly **not live market data**.

---

## 1. What the holdings map actually supports

| Line item | Weight of total portfolio economic exposure | Status |
|---|---|---|
| COIN | 40% | Observed line item |
| HOOD | 30% | Observed line item |
| Unidentified omnibus sleeve | 30% | Composition unknown |
| **Total** | **100%** | Complete only at the *sleeve* level |

The map is **incomplete at the issuer level**. The 40% and 30% are observed line items, not issuer-aggregated totals. The 30% omnibus sleeve may contain additional COIN or HOOD shares, and no issuer-level aggregation is available. I therefore did not submit this to any portfolio risk or concentration calculation, and I am not presenting it as a complete holdings set.

## 2. What the single-issuer policy can and cannot establish

**Policy as stated:** a single issuer breaches only when its issuer-aggregated weight is **greater than 50%**; exactly 50% is not a breach.

**Can establish (deterministic, from observed line items alone):**
- COIN's *observed line item* of 40% is **not** a breach on its own, and cannot be a breach on its own — 40% ≤ 50%.
- HOOD's *observed line item* of 30% is **not** a breach on its own — 30% ≤ 50%.
- Neither observed line item alone can breach the policy, because each is below the threshold before any sleeve allocation.

**Cannot establish:**
- **Whether COIN breaches.** COIN's issuer-aggregated weight is 40% plus any COIN held inside the 30% omnibus sleeve. That aggregate lies in **[40%, 70%]**. The policy outcome is therefore **undetermined**: it breaches if sleeve COIN > 10 percentage points, is exactly at the 50% boundary (no breach) if sleeve COIN = 10 points, and does not breach if sleeve COIN < 10 points.
- **Whether HOOD breaches.** HOOD's aggregate lies in **[30%, 60%]**. It breaches only if sleeve HOOD > 20 percentage points.
- **Whether the two are jointly problematic.** The sleeve cannot simultaneously supply >10 points to COIN and >20 points to HOOD, since it totals 30 points — but this arithmetic bound does not resolve either issuer's status.
- **Any factor, sector, or crypto-beta concentration.** Position weights are not factor exposures. A 70% combined COIN+HOOD line-item weight says nothing about how much of the portfolio's economic exposure is actually driven by crypto prices, and I make no such inference.

**Bottom line:** the policy is *unresolvable* on the supplied data. The correct answer is not "no breach" — it is "cannot be determined without issuer-level aggregation of the omnibus sleeve." Any statement that the portfolio is compliant would be an unsupported claim.

## 3. Screen results — retained and rejected

The screen's 20% reported top-line revenue YoY threshold is a **disclosure filter only**, not the portfolio policy, and the adapter warns that issuer top-line labels differ (total revenue vs. total net revenues) so rates must not be ranked across issuers.

- **Retained — COIN** (Coinbase Global, Inc.), Q3 2024 ended 2024-09-30, released 2024-10-30. Label: `total_revenue`. $1,205,193 thousand vs. $674,148 thousand in Q3 2023 → 78.8% YoY (derived). Also reported: total revenue −17% QoQ, transaction revenue −27% QoQ, net income ~$75 million, pretax crypto investment portfolio loss ~$121 million.
- **Retained — HOOD** (Robinhood Markets, Inc.), Q3 2024 ended 2024-09-30, released 2024-10-30. Label: `total_net_revenues`. $637 million, +36% YoY (reported). Also: net income $150 million, transaction-based revenues $319 million, crypto revenues $61 million (+165% YoY), operating expenses −10% YoY, regulatory accrual $10 million vs. $104 million in Q3 2023.
- **Rejected — SQ** (Block, Inc.), Q3 2024 ended 2024-09-30, released 2024-11-07. Label: `total_net_revenue`. $5.98 billion, +6% YoY — below the 20% disclosure threshold. Also: revenue excluding bitcoin $3.55 billion (+11%), gross profit $2.25 billion (+19%), operating income $323 million, net income attributable to common $284 million. **Rejection is a disclosure-filter outcome, not a judgment on the issuer or on any portfolio weight.** SQ is not a holding in the supplied map.

## 4. Supporting signal and counterpoint from issuer-specific SEC facts

**Supporting signal — both issuers show crypto-linked revenue momentum in the same period, which is why the overlap question matters at all.** For HOOD, crypto revenues were $61 million in Q3 2024, up 165% YoY (HOOD-Q3-CRYPTOREV, HOOD-Q3-CRYPTOREV-YOY), and total net revenues grew 36% YoY to $637 million (HOOD-Q3-NETREV, HOOD-Q3-NETREV-YOY). For COIN, total revenue grew 78.8% YoY to $1,205,193 thousand (COIN-Q3-TOTALREV-2024, COIN-Q3-TOTALREV-2023). Both are Q3 2024, both released 2024-10-30, but the units and labels differ — COIN in USD thousands under `total_revenue`, HOOD in USD millions under `total_net_revenues` — so the two growth rates are **not comparable and must not be ranked**. The useful point is directional and qualitative: two of the three largest observed line items are issuers whose disclosed revenue includes a crypto-sensitive component, which is precisely the situation in which an unaggregated sleeve could hide additional correlated exposure.

**Counterpoint — the same-period disclosures also show that headline growth is not clean, and that COIN's own results contain offsetting items.** COIN's total revenue fell 17% QoQ and transaction revenue fell 27% QoQ (COIN-Q3-REV-QOQ, COIN-Q3-TRANREV-QOQ) while net income was only ~$75 million against a ~$121 million pretax crypto investment portfolio loss (COIN-Q3-NETINCOME, COIN-Q3-CRYPTOLOSS) — so the strong YoY comparison coexists with sequential deterioration and a mark-to-market drag. On the HOOD side, the $150 million net income (HOOD-Q3-NETINCOME) was flattered relative to the prior year by a regulatory accrual falling to $10 million from $104 million (HOOD-Q3-REGACCRUAL, HOOD-Q3-PRIOR-REGACCRUAL) and by operating expenses down 10% YoY (HOOD-Q3-OPEX-YOY) — expense and accrual dynamics, not only revenue, drove the bottom line. Taken together, the counterpoint is that a shared crypto-linked revenue theme does not imply shared or uniform earnings quality, and it certainly does not establish that the portfolio's crypto-factor exposure equals the sum of the two position weights.

## 5. What this analysis does not do

No holdings were invented; the omnibus sleeve remains unidentified. Position weights were not equated with crypto-factor exposure. No return, valuation, price target, or analyst view was inferred — the adapter explicitly excludes share price, valuation, analyst targets, future return, and current market data. No trade was recommended. No thesis, alert, or other ledger record was created or modified.

**Required next input to resolve the policy question:** issuer-level composition of the 30% omnibus sleeve, sufficient to compute COIN and HOOD issuer-aggregated weights. Until then, the single-issuer test is indeterminate for both issuers.
